arxiv-1405-4413.title: Geometric Series as Nontermination Arguments for Linear Lasso Programs
arxiv-1405-4413.creator: Jan Leike, Matthias Heizmann
arxiv-1405-4413.description: Abstract We present a new kind of nontermination argument for linear lasso programs, called geometric nontermination argument . A geometric nontermination argument is a finite representation of an infinite execution of the form ( x → + ∑ i = 0 t λ i ​ y → ) t ≥ 0 (\vec{x}+\sum_{i=0}^{t}\lambda^{i}\vec{y})_{t\geq 0} .

arxiv-2002-03508.title: Fair Correlation Clustering
arxiv-2002-03508.creator: Saba Ahmadi, Sainyam Galhotra, Barna Saha, Schwartz Roy
arxiv-2002-03508.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Saba Ahmadi, Sainyam Galhotra, Barna Saha, Schwartz Roy. In this paper we study the problem of correlation clustering under fairness constraints. In the classic correlation clustering problem, we are given a complete graph where each edge is labeled positive or negative. The goal is to obtain a clustering of the vertices that minimizes disagreements –- the number of of negative edges trapped inside a cluster plus positive edges between different clusters.

arxiv-2112-09724.title: Bass and Betti numbers of a module and its deficiency modules
arxiv-2112-09724.creator: Thiago Fiel, Rafael Holanda
arxiv-2112-09724.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Thiago Fiel, Rafael Holanda. This paper aims to provide several relations between Bass and Betti numbers of a given module and its deficiency modules. Such relations and the tools used throughout allow us to generalize some results of Foxby, characterize Cohen-Macaulay modules in equidimensionality terms, study the Cohen-Macaulay and complete intersection properties of a ring and furnish a case for the Auslander-Reiten conjecture. † † Date: August 8, 2026 † † 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification. Primary 13C14, 13D45; Secondary 13H10, 14B15.

arxiv-2204-09771.title: Relativistic global solutions of neutrino-dominated accretion flows with magnetic coupling 2022
arxiv-2204-09771.creator: Jiao-Zhen She, Tong Liu, Li Xue
arxiv-2204-09771.description: Abstract A Kerr black hole (BH) surrounded by a neutrino-dominated accretion flow (NDAF) is one of plausible candidates of the central engine in gamma-ray bursts. The accretion material might inherit and restructure strong magnetic fields from the compact object mergers or massive collapsars.

arxiv-2301-12858.title: The I = 1 / 2 I=1/2 and 3 / 2 3/2 K- π \pi scattering length with domain wall fermions at physical pion mass with all-to-all propagators
arxiv-2301-12858.creator: Christopher T. Sachrajda
arxiv-2301-12858.description: Abstract We present our calculations for the I = 1 / 2 I=1/2 and 3 / 2 3/2 K- π \pi s-wave scattering length with physical quark masses, extracted from the interaction energy of Euclidean two-point functions. We use the domain wall fermion action with physical quark masses at a single lattice spacing.

arxiv-2310-19963.title: Demonstrating Agreement between Radio and Fluorescence Measurements of the Depth of Maximum of Extensive Air Showers at the Pierre Auger Observatory
arxiv-2310-19963.creator: A. Abdul Halim 13 , P. Abreu 73 , M. Aglietta 55,53 , I. Allekotte 1 , K. Almeida Cheminant 71 , A. Almela 7,12 , R. Aloisio 46,47 , J. Alvarez-Muñiz 79 , J. Ammerman Yebra 79 , G.A. Anastasi 55,53 , L. Anchordoqui 86 , B. Andrada 7 , S. Andringa 73 , Anukriti 76 , L. Apollonio 60,50 , C. Aramo 51 ,
arxiv-2310-19963.description: Abstract We show, for the first time, radio measurements of the depth of shower maximum ( X max X_{\text{max}} ) of air showers induced by cosmic rays that are compared to measurements of the established fluorescence method at the same location.

arxiv-2412-03730.title: Improving Optical Photo- z Estimates Using Submillimeter Photometry Journal: AAS
arxiv-2412-03730.creator: Pouya Tanouri, Ryley Hill, Douglas Scott, Edward L. Chapin
arxiv-2412-03730.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Pouya Tanouri, Ryley Hill, Douglas Scott, Edward L. Chapin. Estimating the redshifts of distant galaxies is critical for determining their intrinsic properties, as well as for using them as cosmological probes. Measuring redshifts spectroscopically is accurate, but expensive in terms of telescope time, hence it has become common to measure ‘photometric’ redshifts, which are fits to photometry taken in a number of filters using templates of galaxy spectral energy distributions (SEDs).

arxiv-2412-07693.title: Leveraging Content and Context Cues for Low-Light Image Enhancement
arxiv-2412-07693.creator: Igor Morawski, Kai He, Shusil Dangi, Winston H. Hsu
arxiv-2412-07693.description: Abstract Low-light conditions have an adverse impact on machine cognition, limiting the performance of computer vision systems in real life. Since low-light data is limited and difficult to annotate, we focus on image processing to enhance low-light images and improve the performance of any downstream task model, instead of fine-tuning each of the models which can be prohibitively expensive.

arxiv-2412-18271.title: OpenMM-Python-Force: Deploying Accelerated Python Modules in Molecular Dynamics Simulation
arxiv-2412-18271.creator: Zhi Wang, Wen Yan
arxiv-2412-18271.description: Abstract We present OpenMM-Python-Force, a plugin designed to extend OpenMM’s functionality by enabling integration of energy and force calculations from external Python programs via a callback mechanism. During molecular dynamics simulations, data exchange can be implemented through torch.Tensor or numpy.ndarray , depending on the specific use case.

arxiv-2509-15646.title: Evidence for Three Subpopulations of Merging Binary Black Holes at Different Primary Masses
arxiv-2509-15646.creator: Sharan Banagiri, Eric Thrane, Paul D. Lasky
arxiv-2509-15646.description: Abstract With the release of the fourth LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA gravitational-wave catalog (GWTC-4), we are starting to gain a detailed view of the population of merging binary black holes. The formation channels of these black holes is not clearly understood, but different formation mechanisms may lead to subpopulations with different properties visible in gravitational-wave data.

arxiv-2601-17816.title: High-Repetition-Rate Projection Multiphoton Lithography for Large-Area Sub-Micron 3D Printing Journal: Journal of Manufacturing Processes
arxiv-2601-17816.creator: S. Papamakarios, M. Manousidaki, M. Stavrou, D. Gray, M. Farsari
arxiv-2601-17816.description: Abstract High-resolution lithographic techniques are often limited by low volumetric throughput, since there is no universal and scalable manufacturing process that can produce 3D metasurfaces. In this work, we demonstrate a high-speed holographic 3D printing platform based on spatiotemporal beam shaping, exceeding the repetition rate while keeping the resolution high.

pmc-11418561.title: Association of herpes simplex virus infection with hearing loss: a cross-sectional study using NHANES data from 2011 to 2012 and 2015 to 2016
pmc-11418561.creator: Yingqiang Li, Bo Su, Xiaodi Wang, Hanqi Chu, Dan Bing
pmc-11418561.description: AbstractObjectivesTo investigate the relationship between herpes simplex virus (HSV) and hearing loss using comprehensive population-based research.DesignThis cross-sectional study utilised data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) to examine the relationship between HSV (types 1 and 2) and hearing loss. The final sample comprised 4608 participants aged 20–49 years.

pmc-11632318.title: Total endovascular arch repair: Initial experience in Bologna
pmc-11632318.creator: Luca Di Marco, Chiara Nocera, Francesco Buia, Francesco Campanini, Domenico Attinà, Giacomo Murana, Luigi Lovato, Davide Pacini
pmc-11632318.description: ObjectivesIn the last few years, fenestrated, branched, or scalloped custom grafts have become available for aortic arch repair. Open surgery is the gold standard, but arch thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) is indicated for high-risk patients. We focused on total endovascular aortic arch replacement with a zone 0 or zone 1 landing zone to describe its short- and long-term outcomes.

pmc-11709562.title: Genome‐wide association analysis and admixture mapping suggest an Alzheimer disease risk locus on chromosome 12 in a Puerto Rican cohort
pmc-11709562.creator: Bilcag Akgun, Briseida E. Feliciano‐Astacio, Joe Rivero, Kara L. Hamilton‐Nelson, Kyle Scott, Katrina Celis, Larry D. Adams, Jose Javier Sanchez, Glenies S Valladares, Concepcion Silva‐Vergara, Vanessa C Rodriguez, Pedro R. Mena, Patrice L. Whitehead, Michael B. Prough, Heriberto Acosta, Anthony J.
pmc-11709562.description: BackgroundHispanic/Latino populations are underrepresented in Alzheimer Disease (AD) genetic studies. The Puerto Rican (PR) population, a three‐way admixed (European, African, and Amerindian) population is the second‐largest Hispanic group in the continental US. We performed a genome‐wide association study (GWAS) in the PR population to identify novel AD susceptibility loci and characterize known AD genetic risk loci.

pmc-11713886.title: Self‐disclosure about dementia on social media: toward evidence‐informed guidance
pmc-11713886.creator: Mahala G English, Mallorie T Tam, Viorica Hrincu, Julie M. Robillard
pmc-11713886.description: BackgroundSocial media platforms are increasingly used by people living with dementia and their care partners to seek information and advice, share personal stories, raise awareness, and offer support to others. Engagement with social media is often accompanied by a personal disclosure of a dementia diagnosis or identification as a care partner, but the impact of this disclosure remains unknown.

pmc-12700870.title: Linking walkability and pedestrian crossing safety using simulated urban environments
pmc-12700870.creator: Anat Meir, Tal Oron-Gilad
pmc-12700870.description: Walking is the most environmentally sustainable mode of transport, offering wide-ranging physical, mental, and ecological benefits. Yet, pedestrian safety remains a critical concern in urban environments. We examined the relationship between pedestrian crossing behaviour and walkability through two complementary stages.

pmc-13336038.title: Heme‐NO Dilates Arteries via Mobilization of NO Moieties From an Intracellular NO Store Within Vascular Smooth Muscle Cells
pmc-13336038.creator: Taiming Liu, Meijuan Zhang, Lingchao Zhu, Haiyan Ke, Amancio de Souza, Qian Li, Daniel Castella, Nicolai Lehnert, Lubo Zhang, Arlin B. Blood
pmc-13336038.description: Nitrosyl heme (heme‐NO) has recently emerged as a surrogate signaling entity for nitric oxide (NO). However, questions remain about how heme‐NO signals across the cell membrane. Herein, we test the hypothesis that extracellular heme‐NO signals as a nitrodilator that vasodilates by mobilizing NO moiety from a nitrodilator‐activated intracellular NO store (NANOS) in the vasculature.

pmc-13579895.title: Hypoxic CA9-high mesenchymal-like glioma stem cells promote ANXA1-FPR1-dependent macrophage polarization in recurrent glioblastoma
pmc-13579895.creator: Hangqi Gao, Guiting You, Jianhuang Huang, Yijing Lin, Jiexin Huang, Risheng Liang, Caihou Lin
pmc-13579895.description: BackgroundRecurrent glioblastoma (rGBM) is characterized by marked myeloid remodeling and a profoundly immunosuppressive microenvironment. Although carbonic anhydrase 9 (CA9) is a canonical hypoxia-inducible molecule linked to aggressive glioblastoma (GBM) behavior, its cell-state-specific distribution in rGBM and its role in glioma stem cell (GSC)-macrophage crosstalk remain incompletely understood.
